channel.description: Recent content in Moe on Best of AI

item.title: Atria Dawn Preview
item.description:
Shanghai AI Laboratory released Atria Dawn Preview on September 11, 2026, an open-weight preview built on a 744-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts foundation and aimed squarely at agentic research and engineering work rather than chat. The design goal is a full loop (problem analysis, tool use, code implementation, running experiments, reading the results, and recovering from failures) rather than answering a question and stopping.

The lab shipped it under an MIT license alongside a 143-author paper studying how the model performed during its own development: across 769 recorded tasks from 56 participants, roughly a third were rated by the humans involved as infeasible without AI assistance.

item.title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
item.description:
DeepSeek shipped V4.1-Flash on September 10, 2026, a 552-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with native vision support and a 1,048,576 token context window that extends to 393,216 tokens of output. Pricing runs on a peak/off-peak split: off-peak rates are $0.003 per million input tokens on a cache hit, $0.15 on a cache miss, and $0.60 per million output tokens, with peak-hour rates (weekday mornings UTC) exactly double.

The tiered pricing is DeepSeek leaning into its usual playbook: undercut Western API pricing hard during low-demand windows to pull in batch and non-latency-sensitive workloads, while still charging enough at peak to manage capacity.

item.title: Hy4 Preview
item.description:
Tencent open-sourced Hy4 Preview on August 28, 2026, a 770-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 49 billion active parameters and a 1 million token context window, released under Apache 2.0. Rather than building a general chat model, Tencent’s Hunyuan team trained it on work data from software engineers, game developers, finance analysts, and security experts, and co-designed it alongside the company’s own CodeBuddy and WorkBuddy products.

In Tencent’s internal blind evaluation, where 163 experts judged 203 real engineering tasks, Hy4 Preview averaged 2.99 out of 4.00, edging out GLM-5.3 at 2.92 and Kimi K3 at 2.94. API pricing runs $0.834 per million input tokens and $2.501 per million output tokens, with cached input at $0.042 per million.

item.title: Ling-3.0-Flash-Fin
item.description:
Ant Group’s InclusionAI team released Ling-3.0-Flash-Fin on August 28, 2026, continuing the training of the base Ling-3.0-Flash model on financial data developed with CICC and other institutions. It keeps the same 124 billion parameter, 5.1 billion active mixture-of-experts design and 256K context window, but adds source-grounded financial search, multi-document reasoning across regulatory filings and earnings reports, and spreadsheet-native valuation work.

Ant published BF16 weights on Hugging Face under an MIT license and opened a one-month free API trial, aiming the model at tasks like reading annual reports, building DCF models, and cross-referencing filings: the kind of grunt work that eats analyst hours at banks and research desks.

item.title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
item.description: Alibaba open-sourced Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on August 26, 2026, giving developers an early look at the Qwen4 architecture ahead of the full model family. It’s a multimodal mixture-of-experts model with a 125 billion parameter backbone but only 6 billion active per token, alongside a 51 billion parameter n-gram embedding table and a 4 billion parameter multi-token prediction module. Context runs natively to 262,144 tokens and extends to a million. Alibaba says it outperforms the older Qwen3.7-Plus, especially on coding and office tasks, while costing roughly one-ninth as much to train and about a twelfth as much to run. Both a standard and an FP8 checkpoint were released at launch.
